- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.33) within 5 days of forecast, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after such events.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often underestimates mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias to account for lingering momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price in the first 7–10 days after a strong upward move — adjust downward by 1–3% in early horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid “over-optimism”.
- Model often ignores sentiment shifts in the 10–15 day window — if sentiment changes direction in that window, adjust forecast by 1–3% to reflect new sentiment trend.
